page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-c1m4.2xlarge is an entry-tier burstable virtual machine belonging to the shared instance family. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base clock of 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance supplies 8 virtual CPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with two threads per core. Memory allocation stands at 32 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Compute resources operate under a shared and burstable scheduling framework, with hypervisor management provided by KVM.

Hardware configurations exclude local storage disks, requiring external cloud disk attachments for persistent volumes. The virtual machine also omits dedicated GPU accelerators. Baseline networking performance is capped at 1 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned directly to the instance. CPU instruction sets include hardware acceleration via AVX-512 foundation and VNNI vector instructions, alongside AES cryptography and bit-manipulation extensions.

Benchmark results demonstrate the behavioral limits of the burstable allocation model. Single-threaded evaluation reveals restrained CPU capacity, marked by a Geekbench single-core score of 884.0 and poor throughput in single-threaded compression tests like gzip (18.68 GB/sec) and bzip3 (6.23 GB/sec). Conversely, aggregated multi-threaded tests align with midrange marks, including a PassMark CPU score of 9221.03, a Geekbench multi-core rating of 4473.0, and 8.5 million Redis SET operations per second. Memory throughput remains steady under load, recording 58.95 GB/sec on uncached read operations.

Cost efficiency is centered on non-sustained compute profiles where full CPU core utilization is intermittent rather than continuous. Given the baseline network bandwidth, burstable CPU constraints, and lack of onboard storage, ecs.t5-c1m4.2xlarge is best matched with development environments, staging servers, lightweight microservices, low-traffic web applications, and internal testing workloads that benefit from 32 GB of memory without requiring sustained core saturation.
